Yellowstone & Grand Teton: a four-day route

Volcanic plateaus, colorful hot springs and fault-block mountains. Start and finish in Bozeman, linking two neighboring yet very different parks through scenic drives, short trails and visitor centers.

Our compact four-day journey

We actually traveled from West Yellowstone through the thermal areas to Grand Teton and back to Yellowstone’s Canyon area in one day. This works as a reference for travelers with limited days who accept an early start and late finish. The route below preserves that journey; time bands are planning estimates, not our recorded arrival times. For relaxed lakeside time, a boat outing or hiking, give Grand Teton a full separate day.

Day 1 | Bozeman → West Yellowstone

After arrival

Collect the rental car, water and next-day picnic supplies. Allow roughly 60–90 minutes, depending on arrival and rental queues.

Afternoon to evening

Drive through Gallatin Canyon to West Yellowstone. Plan roughly 2–2.5 hours on the road, plus stops. On a late arrival, eat and rest rather than adding park visits.

Day 2 | Thermal basins → Grand Teton → back to Yellowstone

06:30–08:15

Depart West Yellowstone; allow for driving and a 30–45-minute Fountain Paint Pot walk. If entry is delayed, reduce later stops.

08:15–09:45

Drive to Old Faithful for the prediction, viewing area and visitor center. Choose whether to wait for an eruption or preserve time for later stops. Omit the longer Morning Glory walk.

09:45–12:00

Drive to Fairy Falls parking and allow 1–2 hours for the Grand Prismatic overlook. Bring lunch; reduce the southbound route if parking or lunch takes longer.

12:00–13:30

Drive to West Thumb for a short lakeside boardwalk walk and lunch buffer. Reassess the southbound and evening return drive; stay in the Yellowstone Lake area if running late.

13:30–15:30

Continue south to Grand Teton, linking Colter Bay, Jackson Lake Dam and Oxbow Bend for brief lake, mountain and river views. This is a compact stretch combining a long drive with quick stops.

15:30–17:00

Visit Jenny Lake’s visitor center and lakeshore, then Mormon Row’s historic barns. Keep visits brief, without a boat trip or waterfall hike. If delayed, choose one of these stops.

17:00–21:00

Return north through West Thumb, Mud Volcano and Hayden Valley toward Canyon. Allow for the drive, brief stops and food; arrival may be later. Wildlife traffic and darkness make driving more demanding. These estimates do not guarantee a full stop everywhere.

Day 3 | Lamar wildlife → Yellowstone canyon → Norris

06:15–11:30

An early-summer example: Morning with the Wild Things wildlife outing. Reserve ahead. Other months may start later, shifting the afternoon accordingly.

11:30–13:00

Lunch in the Canyon area, then the visitor education center for exhibits, stamps and booklet review.

13:00–15:00

Artist Point and one or two north-rim overlooks. Choose short walks and omit the steep Brink of Lower Falls descent.

15:00–17:30

Drive roughly 30 minutes to Norris, then choose Porcelain or part of Back Basin. Both full loops, museums and Artists Paintpots are not all required stops.

17:30–18:30

Return to Canyon for dinner and rest, adding evening views only if time and energy allow.

Day 4｜Mammoth → Gardiner → Bozeman

08:00–10:00

Leave Canyon via Norris for Mammoth. A repeat Artist Point visit needs extra driving and stop time; rainbows are not guaranteed.

10:00–12:00

Choose among a Mammoth terrace walk, seasonal Upper Terrace Drive and Albright Visitor Center according to your walking preferences.

12:00–13:30

Exit north for Roosevelt Arch photos and lunch in Gardiner.

From 13:30

Head to Bozeman, allowing roughly 2–2.5 hours for the road and a buffer, plus fuel, rental return and the airline’s recommended check-in time. With an earlier flight, shorten the morning or stay another night.

Want a fuller Teton visit? Add a fifth day

For a slower pace, stay in the Grand Teton or Jackson area after heading south on day two. Give the next full day to Jenny Lake’s shore and visitor center plus Mormon Row, then return north to Yellowstone. Shift wildlife and the northern route by one day. Reserve another half day for a boat-and-hike outing. This is an optional extension; lodging is listed by area and seasonal activities need reservations.

Official information & before you go

This route is for the season when main roads are open. Times are planning estimates, not guarantees, and do not include every parking, traffic or weather delay. Check seasonal roads, trails and visitor-center hours before departure.
